added.title: A diagram whole marks a return-loop or branch junction

screening: IDEA000041 passed ideas duplicates with no same declared design and route-check. It is related to IDEA000035 (instrument/endpoint) and IDEA000039 (component/state key), but its target unit and falsifier are graph topology: return/junction enrichment versus terminal or owner/component association.

self_challenge.rivals_mutually_exclusive: Not inherently. A single locus could be both a component/state key and a return junction. The proposed test therefore requires an interaction model or held loci where topology and component/owner are separately coded; a raw topology association alone cannot choose the meanings.
self_challenge.physical_event_overlap: Yes. One physical return-loop event can satisfy instrument, component, endpoint, and topology descriptions. These are rival projections requiring independent controls, not mutually exclusive observations.
self_challenge.counts_renderer_generated: No manuscript count is claimed. GDT209 directly reports two connected vessels, one return-loop vessel, paired ducts, and side outlets; these are source-observed comparator facts. No renderer-generated frequency is used.
self_challenge.source_quote_type: Observation in the comparator report, not Voynich semantic binding. Independent graph, owner, component, and topology endpoints remain unknown.
self_challenge.smallest_decisive_step: Predeclare a held diagram-locus table with topology class, owner, component class, and complete form, then test topology enrichment against owner/component and endpoint nulls without treating the historical comparator as label evidence.

rejected_candidates.reason: Rejected as a new intake because it collapses into IDEA000040 treatment-mode/flow scope and would use a comparator prediction rather than a distinct source observation.
